tools.name: save_search_alert
tools.description: Use this when a buyer wants to hear about works listed later that match what they are looking for. It saves the search — the buyer’s words in query and the same filters as search_artworks — and tells the buyer by e-mail, or your own system by webhook, when a work that matches it is listed: only work

tools.name: get_search_alert
tools.description: Use this when a buyer asks about an alert for new works they saved: whether it is waiting for them to confirm it, active or ended, what it watches, when it last sent works and when it ends. Needs the search_alert_id and manage_token save_search_alert gave.

tools.name: cancel_search_alert
tools.description: Use this when a buyer wants to stop an alert for new works. Nothing more is sent, and the saved words, filters and address are erased. Needs the search_alert_id and manage_token save_search_alert gave; a buyer can also stop it from any alert e-mail in one click.

tools.description: Use this when a buyer asks what a work will cost delivered to them and when it would arrive. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp?surface=registry" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_artworks, get_artwork · Private data: get_order_status, open_claim · Public sink: search_artworks, save_search_alert · Destructive: get_artwork.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_artworks, get_artwork · Private data: get_order_status, open_claim · Public sink: search_artworks, save_search_alert · Destructive: get_artwork

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_artworks" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
